title: Mounts, bags and light bikepacking loads
summary: Understand what frame and fork mounting points enable, where their limits come from, and how added luggage changes the bicycle.

steps.title: Purpose-built mounts provide defined attachment points.
steps.body: Threaded frame and fork bosses let compatible cages or accessories attach without improvised clamps around the structure.
steps.keyFact: A threaded hole does not imply unlimited load or compatibility with every accessory.

steps.title: Fork-mounted cargo affects steering.
steps.body: Mass attached to the fork moves with steering and can change steering feel. The allowed mass, bolt length and accessory type depend on the actual fork and mounting system.
steps.keyFact: Bike Atlas does not infer cargo capacity from the number of visible fork bosses.

steps.title: Rough surfaces expose the lower frame to debris.
steps.body: A downtube protector adds a replaceable or sacrificial layer against abrasion and smaller debris impacts. It does not make the frame immune to structural damage.
steps.keyFact: Protection reduces exposure; impact damage still requires inspection of the underlying frame.

steps.title: Where luggage sits matters as much as how much it weighs.
steps.body: Added mass changes acceleration, braking and handling. Loads attached high, far forward or asymmetrically can feel different from compact loads centered within the frame.
steps.keyFact: Use the documented limits of every real mounting interface and test loaded handling in a controlled environment.

challenge.prompt: What determines the allowable load on a Gravel G1-style mounting point?

options.label: The actual frame/fork, fastener and accessory specifications
The number of visible mounting bolts

challenge.explanation: Load capacity is defined by the actual mounting system and its documented limits.
